findings.reason: CCN34 holds, across53 nonblank lines with nesting2. This is one ordered priority policy: validate numeric scores, use rubric order for ties, take the lowest score first, incorporate growGoal/nextTime, supplement scores at or below8 while maintaining a two-category minimum, consider computed Flow only with space, and finish with grounded default categories. The local addPriority operation centralizes normalization/deduplication. The checklist policy nearby is not interchangeable: its threshold and two-action limit deliberately differ. Tests explicitly preserve ties, numeric zero, legacy goal precedence, score8 inclusion and the two-category minimum. No small shared operation removes these decisions; splitting ranking or goal fields into one-use helpers relocates policy and fallback precedence without eliminating duplication.

findings.reason: CCN33 is accurate. The decisions enforce candidate sanitization, maximum examples, priority membership, distinct quotes/categories and staged fallback. In particular, a rejected duplicate must keep searching within the required category, required categories precede general candidates, and duplicate-quote fallback is permitted under narrower rules than ordinary selection. Existing addNotebookGuideFallbackExample cannot replace addExample unchanged: it lacks the maximum/priority/category-duplication checks and has different acceptance rules. Generalizing it would expand its signature/options and alter a second selection path. No equivalence-preserving simplification with a net readability gain was identified. Keep these policy decisions; the separate prototype-key lead needs a regression and does not make this complexity marker false.

additional_leads.relation_to_assigned_findings: Separate behavior lead noticed while checking quote deduplication and validator dependencies. It does not make the nine shape metrics false and is not a scanner clearance.
additional_leads.reason: The arbitrary quote-key map seen starts as {} and checks seen[key] before an example is added. A first quote key __proto__ therefore appears previously seen through Object.prototype and is rejected on ordinary required/general passes. Separately, getNotebookGuideContentWords uses a {} stopWords table with !stopWords[word]; the lower-case English word constructor is inherited and silently excluded although it is not in the declared stop-word list. Both are source-supported dictionary membership leads, not reproduced failures in this read-only review.

additional_leads.regression_recommendation: After the publication gate, extend the existing local native notebook-guidance harness. First assert getNotebookGuideContentWords("constructor") retains that word and a grounded constructor-only quote can pass sanitization. Independently use source containing a bounded __proto__ identifier and a concrete same-word revision such as "The __proto__ value"; assert sanitization accepts it before assembly, then assert the first candidate is retained. Keep ordinary duplicate-quote/category rejection, required-category order, bounds and fallback cases. Confirm actual old-app failures before editing. Candidate minimal operations are an own-property stop-word lookup in getNotebookGuideContentWords and a prototype-free arbitrary quote map in assembleNotebookGuideFromCandidates; inspect the fallback quote-map caller contract before choosing complete scope. The stop-word operation is outside the four named functions and needs explicit coordinator scope for a repair.
